name: Protocols.io
description: The premier open-access repository for interactive, step-by-step scientific methods. It hosts living, updatable instructions for physical lab setups, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and computational pipeline workflows.

name: Protocol Exchange
description: Sponsored by Nature Portfolio, this is a completely open preprint server and repository for community-contributed laboratory instructions covering all natural sciences.

name: OSF (Open Science Framework)
description: A massive open-source project management hub for all sciences. It lets you host structured data, build lab wikis for procedural documentation, and natively integrates with code repositories like GitHub or GitLab. Every public project gets a dedicated DOI (Digital Object Identifier).

name: Code Ocean
description: A specialized computational platform that uses 'Compute Capsules'. It bundles scientific code, data dependencies, and the exact software execution environment together, ensuring any scientist can reproduce a web or lab computation instantly.

name: Galaxy Project
description: An open-source, web-based database and platform for data-intensive scientific research. It allows scientists to run highly complex computational analyses and sharing code workflows without needing advanced local hardware.

name: Papers with Code
description: Though highly geared towards AI, it traces computational code, benchmark datasets, and scientific research papers across medical, physical, and computational sciences to show you exactly how a data model was processed.

name: Materials Cloud
description: An open platform for computational materials science that stores the exact simulation pipelines, source codes, and raw data graphs, allowing you to retrace every calculated result.

name: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR)
description: A meticulously curated database blending physiological, bioimaging, and environmental scientific data with code analysis pipelines.
